In [[formal language]] theory, a '''picture language''' is a set of ''pictures'', where a picture is a 2D array of characters over some alphabet.

For example, the language <math>L = \left \{ a^{n,n+1} \mid n > 0 \right \} </math> defines the language of rectangles composed of the character <math>a</math>.  This language <math>L</math> contains pictures such as:

<math>\begin{pmatrix}a\\a\end{pmatrix},
\begin{pmatrix} a&a\\a&a\\a&a\end{pmatrix},
\begin{pmatrix} a&a&a\\a&a&a\\a&a&a\\a&a&a\end{pmatrix}
\in L</math>

The study of picture languages was initially motivated by the problems of pattern recognition and image processing, but two-dimensional patterns also appear in the study of [[cellular automaton|cellular automata]] and other [[parallel computing]] models.  Some [[formal system]]s have been created to define picture languages, such as array grammars and tiling systems.
